newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine judge annuls Menem labor decrees-reports.
newsitem.headline: Argentine judge annuls Menem labor decrees-reports.

text.p: An Argentine judge who had suspended President Carlos Menem's three labor reform decrees has now declared them null and void, one local news agency and a television channel reported Tuesday.
Labor Judge Ines Gassibe froze the decrees last week on a petition from the CGT trade union federation, following a ruling by another labor judge that the decrees violated the constitution.
The ruling of "non-applicability" backs up an initial decision by Labor Judge Julio Garcia Martinez earlier this month that the decrees signed by Menem in late December are unconstitutional.

Judge Gassibe, who had ordered their suspension pending a full explanation by the government, was quoted by local news agency DyN saying that "our constitution...consecrates unions' guaranteed right to arrange collective labor agreements."

Menem's decrees would let smaller firms bypass national unions in collective pay talks and let firms appeal to the government if they want to negotiate with trade unions on a company-by-company and not an industry-wide basis.
Overturning such a right by decree violates norms of the Geneva-based International Labor Organization, Gassibe said.

Menem, who argues that the "flexibilization" of labor laws is the best way to tackle 17.3 percent unemployment, resorted to presidential decrees in the face of opposition in Congress and a breakdown in negotiations with unions, who fear their power is under threat. The CGT staged a 24-hour general strike on December 26, its third in the year.

Labor Minister Armando Caro Figueroa formally replied last Friday to Judge Gassibe, saying the government stood by the legitimacy of the decrees. The government had been working on a further batch of labor reform decrees.
